When initialising an event
ensure that the PMU's module cannot be removed for the lifetime of the
event
column2: with __free_event() dropping the reference when the event is

column1: finally destroyed. If something fails after the event has been
initialised
column2: but before the event is installed

column1: drop the reference on the module.
However
column2: if we fail to initialise an event for some reason (e.g. we ask

column1: an uncore PMU to perform sampling
column2: and it refuses to initialise the

column1: event)
column2: we do not drop the refcount. If we try to open such a bogus

column1: event without a precise IDR type
column2: we will loop over each PMU in the pmus

column1: list
column2: incrementing each of their refcounts without decrementing them.

column1: This patch adds a module_put when pmu->event_init(event) fails
that the refcounts are balanced in failure cases. As the innards of the
precise and search based initialisation look very similar
hoisted out into a new helper function. While the early return for the
failed try_module_get is removed from the search case
by the remaining return when ret is not -ENOENT.
